Unchanged, but declared deliberate at the site: well_viewer/features/home/cell_gating/gating_compute.py:322-333 `_cell_gating_valid_mask` and :422-428 `_valid_values_for_channel` both state that the fluorescence `Included` gate is *deliberately* not applied because the CDFs and optimizer are the surface for SETTING that gate and filtering by it would be circular. All three branches of well_viewer/features/barplot/collect.py now spell it `has_frac = not math.isnan(...)` uncoupled from `has_mean` — pooled/grouped at :537, per-well at :705, member branch at :951 — each with a comment explaining that a fraction of 0 is a measurement. (The uncoupling was briefly at risk in commit 598ebb01 but survived, with a guard added.)

`bar_err_settings` (well_viewer/features/barplot/collect.py:1310) has exactly one consumer, barplot/controller.py:184 (the aggregate path). The per-cell Events panel, `draw_per_well_n_bars` in well_viewer/features/barplot/renderer.py:1212, never calls it: it draws an errorbar at :1295 on the raw `if err_val > 0` test with no `draw_err` gate and no `ci_scale` multiplier, so "None" and "95 % CI" still apply to grouped mode only. Judged a false positive and reverted. well_viewer/features/qc/tab_view.py:161-183 `_fields_params` passes the raw box text to `QCParams(...).with_updates(**bounds)` so `qc_params._pos` (domain/qc_params.py:46) normalises 0/blank/negative to None, and the docstring states why: for a QC *maximum* zero means no bound (a `max_area == 0` would exclude every cell), and for a minimum it keeps the same population either way. Commit 598ebb01 records that the earlier falsy-zero 'fix' blanked every plot.

well_viewer/domain/fold_change.py:94 `_as_finite` is now a duck-typed `float(value)` conversion (bools excluded), and the module imports `is_number` from the new well_viewer/domain/numeric.py at :71, used at ~20 guard sites (:157, :473, :728, :997, :1474, :1749 ...). numeric.py rejects anything sized so a 1-element array cannot sneak through as a scalar.

well_viewer/features/export/service.py:155-157 — `line_metric_row` writes the spread as `f"{spread:.6f}" if is_number(spread) else ""`, with a comment saying an empty cell rather than the string "nan" because a spreadsheet reads a literal nan as text; the events spread at :162-166 is blanked the same way, matching `bar_metric_row`'s `_num` helper.

The named site is fixed: well_viewer/domain/ratio_models.py:24-33 now says epsilon is "the floor the denominator is clamped to ... not a term added to it (np.maximum(den, epsilon))" and explains the sign-flip near zero. But the same wrong claim survives at two siblings — the resolver's own docstring, well_viewer/data/data_loading.py:470 ("returns ``num / (den + epsilon)``"), immediately above the clamping code at :495-496, and the user-facing Ratios tab text at well_viewer/features/home/ratios/tab_view.py:53-57 ("numerator / (denominator + ε)" / "a small constant added to the denominator").

well_viewer/features/smfish/worker.py:350-377 — `_write_counts_to_csvs` returns `written` (:154-225), the caller computes `shortfall = total - written`, passes it to `after_csv_cb(shortfall)` (signature widened; the one live caller, features/smfish/tab_view.py:1004, takes it), and `done_cb` reports "Apply to All wrote N of M well(s) ..." with an early return instead of the unconditional "complete" message. well_viewer/runtime_app.py:213 `teardown_review_pane` calls `stop_runtime_workers(runtime, "cell_gating", ("worker", "auto_worker"))` (core/worker_bridge.py:165 — cancel() then a bounded wait). `_AutoThresholdWorker` now has a cancel flag: features/home/cell_gating/controller.py:846 `_cancelled`, :859 `cancel()`, :884 `should_cancel=` and :898/:902 refusing to emit once cancelled; both restart paths cancel-then-wait(50) first (:795-804, :940-956).

well_viewer/features/smfish/worker.py:288-324 — the executor is no longer a `with` block; the `finally` calls `executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)`, so a cancel drops every not-yet-started well instead of decoding the plate. Residual, unchanged and by design: all wells are still submitted up front, and the outer thread (:391, `daemon=True`) is returned to the caller rather than joined — teardown_review_pane sets the cancel event instead, so shutdown cannot block on it.

well_viewer/domain/spatial_compute.py:224 — `seen = set(nbrs)` is built once per cluster before the expansion loop and maintained incrementally at :233-235; the per-core-point rebuild is gone and the comment records the measurement.
